ui._comment: English source. Keys never change; translate the values. {name} placeholders are filled in by the app; keep them. Keys ending in _html may contain simple HTML tags such as <em>.
ui.brand.tagline: A card game for scientists. Read the research claim, then flag its reasoning error, or call it sound.
ui.lang.label: Language
ui.footer: Red Flag v{version}, part of the SMART-Lab Science Game Kit. Claim cards are constructed teaching examples; the real cases are on the Flag cards, each with its source. The key has three tiers because reasonable readers disagree: argue with it.
ui.home.title_html: Spot the flaw, or trust the evidence.
ui.home.lede: Every claim card is a headline, an abstract sentence or a small chart. Play the Flag that names its reasoning error, or call it sound. About one claim in four is sound, and false alarms cost points.
ui.home.play.text: One claim at a time: pick the right Flag from four cards, or the Sound card. Then name the Check that exposes it for a bonus point.
ui.home.decks.text: Every Claim, Flag and Check card, with the answer key, a real historical case for each Flag and the paper that defines it.
ui.quick.title: Flawed or sound?
ui.quick.text: Flip the card, read the claim, then make your call.
ui.tip.claims: Research claims: headlines, abstract sentences and small charts. Most overreach in one typical way; about one in four is sound.
ui.tip.flags: Reasoning errors in research, from correlation as causation to forking paths. Play one on a claim to name what is wrong with it.
ui.tip.checks: The move that exposes a flag, such as 'Ask for the denominator'. Advanced players add one to their Flag for a bonus point.
ui.tip.sound: Play it when the claim holds up: its evidence supports what it says, and no more. Calling a flawed claim sound costs points, and so does flagging a sound one.
ui.play.which: Which Flag fits this claim, or is it sound?
ui.play.tap_hint: Tap a card to read it full size, then pick it.
ui.play.step1_b: Read the claim, then the conclusion.
ui.play.step1: What does it say, and what does the evidence actually show?
ui.play.step2: Cause from a correlation, people from groups, a big claim from a small sample?
ui.play.step3: Some claims are sound. A false alarm costs as much as a missed flaw.
ui.play.false_flag: This claim is sound: its evidence supports what it says. Flagging it is a false alarm.
ui.play.missed: This claim has a flaw, so calling it sound lets it through.
ui.verdict.unlisted: Unlisted. At a table you could appeal
ui.review.label: Bonus: the check
ui.review.which_sound: Which Check card confirms that this claim is sound?
ui.review.wrong: ❌ Not that one. The key check is
ui.ref.title: Key reference: {cite}
ui.card.flag_or_sound: Flag it or call it sound
ui.card.sound_text: The evidence supports what the claim says, and no more. No flag applies.
ui.card.sound_penalty: {trap} if the claim has a flaw
ui.card.trap_note: Flagging a sound claim, or calling a flawed one sound, is always a trap.
ui.card.appeal: {unlisted}, or +{appeal} if the table upholds your appeal
ui.card.check_bonus: +{check} if your Check card exposes your Flag on this claim
ui.card.round1: Flip the top Claim card. Everyone reads it.
ui.card.round2: Race to slap down the Flag that names its error, or your Sound card. First card down claims the call.
ui.card.round3: Advanced: add the Check card that would expose your Flag.
ui.card.round4: Read the key aloud: score, argue, appeal. Next player flips.
ui.print.title: {game}: print and play
ui.print.intro: {tagline} Version {version}. {total} cards in standard poker size (63 × 88 mm), 9 per A4 page.
ui.print.printing_html: Printing. Print at 100% / actual size with background graphics on. Cut along the card edges. All cards share one back (backs.html): print it on the reverse of each sheet, or skip it and use opaque card sleeves.
ui.print.answers_html: Answers are in the separate answer-key booklet (answer-key.html), so the top card of a face-down deck never gives its answer away.
ui.print.key_intro: 🥇 best +3 · 🥈 defensible +1 · ⚠️ trap −2 · unlisted 0 (appeal for +1) · matching Check +1. On a sound claim every flag is a trap; on a flawed claim, calling it sound is a trap. Read the why aloud: that is where the learning happens.
